title: The Coherence Imperative

canonical_node.axiom: Coherence is measurable, necessary, and the basis of all structure; order is a fundamental feature of reality's architecture.
definitions: Coherence C[chi] = 1 - (S_observed / S_maximum), measuring organized information density.
Order: the degree of organization in information, with Order(I) > 0 for meaning.
Parsimony: nature prefers minimal description, formalized as dK/dt = -chi(t).
Decoherence: local decrease in coherence, representing information degradation, not destruction.
derivation: Information exists and requires a substrate (from F02).
Not all information is equal; some carries meaning, some is noise.
Therefore, coherence is the condition for meaning.
Coherence is measurable via entropy, and nature prefers minimal description, as evidenced by elegant physical laws.
canonical_node.action: Treat coherence as a fundamental, measurable property; use C[chi] to assess order in systems; recognize that local decoherence is degradation but information is conserved.
boundary: Does not claim to prove the existence of God or specific theological doctrines.
Does not assert that coherence is conserved in all cases; only in closed systems.
Does not provide a complete physical theory; it is a conceptual framework.
test: Verify that C[chi] is non-negative and well-defined for given systems.
Check that local coherence can increase at the expense of the environment.
Assess whether physical laws exhibit parsimony (low Kolmogorov complexity).

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a quantitative measure of order (coherence) and links it to meaning, parsimony, and physical structure.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the foundational role of information and its substrate from F02.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without coherence, information cannot be meaningful, undermining the entire framework of ordered reality.

overstatement_risks: Claims coherence is fundamental without rigorous proof.
Equates theological coherence with physical coherence without justification.
Uses fine-tuning arguments that are contested.
Asserts parsimony as a law of nature rather than a heuristic.
kill_conditions: If meaning can exist without organization.
If coherence cannot be measured in practice.
If nature does not prefer parsimony.
risk.lean_target: Formalize coherence as a measurable quantity in information theory, but avoid theological overreach.

plain_summary: This document argues that coherence (order) is fundamental and measurable, using entropy-based definitions and parsimony. It critiques chaos, random universe, and entropy-only views. However, it lacks rigorous proof and mixes theology with physics, so it is not established as a formal result.
